The present Detailed Accidental Report was filed qua the accident dated 30.09.2020.As per the facts of the present case on 30.09.2020, at about 09.40 p.m near Gouri Ganesh Apartment and Balaji Apartment a Tata 909 bearing No.HR 63D1194 being driven in very high speed and in rash and negligent manner hit the scooty being driven by the deceased ( Lalit Miglani) .
As a result of which the scooty came under TATA 909 and the rider of the scooty received multiple grievous injuries.
The deceased was taken to Akash Health Care Center, Sec.3 Dwarka by the PCR for his treatment where he has expired during treatment.

sentences.text: 2. After investigation, investigating agency contended that said accident took place, due to rash and negligent driving of Tata 909 bearing No.HR63D1194 being driven by Jagveer (driver), who has been made respondent no. 1.
Sh Mukesh Kumar (owner) was made respondent no. 2 and Liberty General Insurance Company Limited was made as respondent no. 3.
The present DAR has been filed by the IO.
The DAR has been considered as claim application.
3. The respondent No.1 and 2 have not filed any W.S on their behalf.
4. The respondent no. 3 (insurance company) has filed its WS stating therein that accident has occurred due to the negligence of deceased while driving the scooty.

My issuewise findings are as under: ISSUE No.(i) Whether Lalit Miglani sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated on 30.09.2020 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. 8.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.

To prove this fact petitioners examined PW2 HC Sandeep as material witness, who has deposed that on 30.09.2020, at about 09.40 p.m when he was on duty near Gouri Ganesh Apartment and Balaji Apartment.
A Tata 909 bearing No.HR63D1194 being driven in very high speed and in rash and negligent manner hit the scooty being driven by the deceased .
He has deposed that the scooty came under TATA 909 and the rider of the scooty received multiple grievous injuries.
The deceased was taken to Akash Health Care Center, Sec.3 Dwarka by the PCR 9.

sentences.text: Ld Counsel for the Insurance Company has argued that PW2 is not trustworthy witness qua to fact that he was the witness of accident.

It is submitted that there are material contradictions in the cross examination of PW.2.
10.

After considering the submission of Ld Counsel for the Insurance Company and perusal of testimony of PW2, it reveals that there is no contradiction at all in the testimony of PW2 which can make him disbelievable.
PW2 was posted as Constable at the place of accident and witnessed the accident.
Even otherwise, he is also a witness in the investigation for the offence U/S 279/304A IPC.
Moreover the proof of negligence, while disposing off a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/304A of IPC.
The charge sheet was filed against respondent no.1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against his such implication.

Considering all the evidence as discussed above, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of a Tata 909 bearing No.HR63D1194 being driven by respondent no.1 thereby causing death of Lalit Miglani 11.

This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that victim Lalit Miglani died in a motor vehicle accident due to rash and negligent driving of Tata 909 bearing No.HR63D1194 by respondent no.1.
ISSUE No.2: Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?

OPP.
12.
Petitioner no.1 and 2 are the wife and mother of victim ( deceased Lalit Miglani) as such LRs of victim.
They are entitled for claim.

Now coming to the extent of compensation.
PW 1 ,wife of the deceased has deposed that at the time of accident her husband was doing the private business in Delhi and earning Rs.50,000/ p.m.
On the other hand, Ld Counsel for the Insurance company that there is no evidence qua proving monthly income of the petitioner.

However Ld Counsel for the petitioner fairly admitted that he has not placed on record any document qua showing the income of petitioner and submits that income of the petitioner may be assessed as per Minimum Wages Act.
On perusal, as per Degree being issued by University of Delhi Ex PW1/2 ( Colly), the deceased was Graduate from University of Delhi.

So this Tribunal while assessing the income of deceased under Minimum Wages Act prevailing in Delhi has assessed the income of deceased for the computation of compensation under the head of Graduate as Rs.19,572/ p.m.
14.

As per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others of Hon'ble Supreme Court the net income of the deceased is to be counted after deduction of tax and future benefit have to be given @ 25%.

sentences.text: 15. There are two L.Rs of deceased ie his wife and moher, at the time of accident, so deceased spending 1/3rd of his income on his personal expenses.
Therefore the income for the purpose of loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs.16,310/ (19,572/ + 4,893/  8,155/) per month.
16. To calculate loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased.
The age of the deceased was 42 years old at the time of accident ( 05.05.1978, as per Aadhar Card )
A multiplier of 14 is thus taken in calculating loss of dependency.
Counting in this way, loss of dependency comes to Rs. 27,40,080/ (16,310/ x 12 x 14).
This amount of Rs. 27,40,080/ is allowed to petitioner no.1 and 2 as loss of dependency.
